findings.title: New exit-code behavior (4 for disabled feature, 3 for recreate) is not asserted in tests
findings.body: The PR changes the RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces exit code 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED), and documents both in update-compatibility.adoc. However, no test asserts these exit codes: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error text, and testWrongVersions only checks the error messages without asserting exit code 3. Since the documented exit-code contract is the primary interface for automation pipelines, a regression in the codes would go unnoticed. Add assertEquals(4, result.exitCode()) in testFeatureNotEnabled and assertEquals(3, ...) after the incompatible-version runs.

findings.title: Disabled feature exit code 4 is ambiguous for scripts that only check non-zero as 'recreate needed'
findings.body: The guide now says the check command fails with exit code 4 when the rolling-updates feature is disabled, while exit code 3 means 'rolling upgrade not possible, recreate required'. A pipeline that treats any non-zero-but-not-error exit as 'do a recreate upgrade' (a natural reading of the documented table since both 3 and 4 are 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible') would silently shut down the deployment because the operator forgot to enable the feature, rather than failing loudly. The doc should explicitly warn that exit code 4 must be treated as a configuration error, not as a recreate signal.
